summary: End-to-end ML platforms combine training, fine-tuning, experiment tracking, model registry, feature stores, and deployment/serving into a managed environment, differing from a simple model API in that they let you build, govern, and operate your own models at scale rather than just calling someone else's. You need a full platform when you train or heavily fine-tune proprietary models, require data governance and reproducible MLOps, or serve models at enterprise scale; a hosted model API suffices when you only need inference from a pre-built foundation model. In 2026 the landscape is converging—cloud-native suites (SageMaker, Vertex AI, Azure ML) compete with data-centric platforms (Databricks) and specialized MLOps/compute tools (W&B, Modal), with SageMaker leading by raw customer count due to AWS's footprint and Databricks winning data-team-led purchases.

platforms.name: Amazon SageMaker AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute instance-hour for training, inference endpoints, and storage; no upfront cost, with savings plans available
platforms.best_for: Engineering-team-led purchases and organizations already standardized on AWS needing deep native infrastructure integration

platforms.name: Databricks (MLflow + Mosaic AI)
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based pricing via Databricks Units (DBUs) on top of underlying cloud compute; tiered by workload type
platforms.best_for: Data-team-led purchases wanting a unified lakehouse plus ML/GenAI platform with strong governance across clouds

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per node-hour for training and prediction, plus per-token pricing for foundation models
platforms.best_for: Teams on Google Cloud wanting tight integration with BigQuery, Gemini models, and AutoML

platforms.name: Azure Machine Learning
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per compute instance; no surcharge over underlying Azure VM pricing, with reserved capacity options
platforms.best_for: Enterprises standardized on Microsoft/Azure stack needing governance and Azure OpenAI integration

platforms.name: Weights & Biases
platforms.pricing: Free tier for individuals; per-seat/usage subscription for teams and enterprise with self-hosted options
platforms.best_for: ML research and engineering teams needing best-in-class experiment tracking and model lineage across any training stack

platforms.name: DataRobot
platforms.pricing: Enterprise subscription/licensing (custom quote); consumption and platform tiers
platforms.best_for: Enterprises and analysts wanting automated model building and governance with less hands-on coding

platforms.name: MLflow
platforms.pricing: Free and open source; managed hosting available via Databricks or cloud vendors
platforms.best_for: Teams wanting an open-source, vendor-neutral experiment tracking and model registry standard

platforms.name: H2O.ai
platforms.pricing: Open-source core (H2O-3) free; Driverless AI and enterprise GenAI products via commercial license
platforms.best_for: Organizations wanting AutoML plus open-source flexibility and on-prem/private GenAI deployments

platforms.name: Kubeflow
platforms.pricing: Free and open source; cost is the underlying Kubernetes infrastructure
platforms.best_for: Platform teams wanting a self-managed, Kubernetes-native ML stack with full control and portability

platforms.name: Modal
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-second serverless compute billing for CPU/GPU usage; free starter credits
platforms.best_for: AI startups and teams wanting fast, code-first serverless GPU execution without managing infrastructure
